method: Read the a/b grounds files, the CSS of a.html/a-home.html and b.html/b-home.html, all eight web and mobile screenshots and checks/report.json, and computed WCAG 2 contrast ratios for every token pair the CSS applies (text on panel, side/table-header grounds, the SVG diagram grounds, control borders, the logo against its ground).

entries.reason: Every ground is a dark tint of Manage's page blue #467495 (page #0b1318, panel #15232d), the navbar stays Manage green #5d8108 with the #7b9f0e accent, and headings stay blue/green, so it reads as iHRIS at night. The blue cast is subtle but present on every surface, including mobile.

At 1280 the layout, sidebar, field table, neighbourhood diagram and home cards all render with clear hierarchy and no overflow. Panel against page is only 1.17:1, so the page gutter barely separates from the content column, but this does not affect reading.

At 390 the field rows stack into bordered cards, the menu button and search are 44px targets, and the relationship lists replace the diagram, all legible on the dark-blue panel with no horizontal scroll.

Body text is 8.35:1 on the panel and 7.01:1 on the side/table-header ground, and headings, links and muted text are about 5.4:1 on the panel. However, sidebar links (#009deb on #1d313e) come to 4.498:1, just under 4.5, and the diagram's base-class label (#bbbbbb on #315168) is 4.36:1.

This is the hue-faithful alternative to B's neutral charcoal. The trade-off is clear: brand presence on every surface, against a less neutral reading ground. Inverting the logo, rather than tiling it, is a reasonable way to keep it visible.

The panel is neutral charcoal (#1a1a1a), so Manage's page blue survives only in the 20px gutters at 1280 and disappears entirely at 390 (the wrap fills the viewport). iHRIS identity then rests on the green navbar and the blue/green headings alone. It still reads as iHRIS, but less recognisably than A.
Same layout as A with no overflow. The grey panel, #262626 table headers and #474747 rules give clean, neutral separation, and the data tables read very well.
Stacked field cards, 44px menu, search and link targets, and collapsible relationship lists are all legible at 390 with no horizontal scroll.

Body text is 8.12:1 on the panel and 7.06:1 on side/header grounds, links and headings are 4.50-5.20:1, and control borders are 3.33-3.83:1. However, the diagram's base-class label (#b1b1b1 on #474747) is 4.33:1, under the 4.5 target. The white logo tile gives the black mark 17.4:1 and keeps its original colours.

This is a genuine alternative to A: a neutral reading ground with brand colour kept at the edges, plus a white tile behind the logo instead of an inverted mark. The comparison shows the brand-versus-neutrality trade-off clearly.

factualIssues.issue: Sidebar navigation links use --link #009deb on --side-bg #1d313e, which gives 4.498:1, just below the 4.5:1 target for normal text (the 13-15px links are not large text). Raising the link lightness slightly fixes it.

Neighbourhood SVG: the base-class box label (I2CE_List) is --diagram-ink #bbbbbb on --diagram-base #315168, 4.36:1, below 4.5 (the 12px SVG text also renders smaller than 12px once scaled). A muted fill (#969696) on the diagram base would be 2.83:1.
Neighbourhood SVG: the base-class box label (I2CE_List) is --diagram-ink #b1b1b1 on --diagram-base #474747, 4.33:1, below 4.5. A muted fill (#8c8c8c) on the diagram base would be 2.76:1.
At mobile width no surface carries Manage's page blue (#1a2b38 shows only in the desktop gutters), so 'page blue kept at the edges' does not hold on phones.

Several pairs sit exactly at the 4.5:1 floor on the #262626 ground (h1 4.496:1, h3 and muted text 4.50:1). h1 is not placed on that ground in these pages, but there is no margin left for rounding or anti-aliasing.

Rules and card/A-Z borders (#315168 on #15232d) are 1.91:1. They are decorative separators, and the A-Z links' text identifies them, so this is acceptable. The real input borders meet 3:1 (#777777 is 3.58:1 on the panel and 3.00:1 on the side ground).
